subject: Anatomy
summary: The femoral nerve supplies the anterior thigh muscles and gives sensation to the medial thigh and knee. It emerges from L2‑L4, travels under the inguinal ligament, and is vulnerable to injury in hip fractures and surgical procedures.

sections.p: The femoral nerve is the largest branch of the lumbar plexus, carrying motor and sensory fibers that control thigh flexion and knee extension, and provide cutaneous sensation to the medial thigh.
It exits the pelvis through the psoas major, runs anterior to the iliac vessels, and pierces the inguinal ligament into the thigh.
b: Course: psoas major → iliac fossa → inguinal ligament → thigh

t.b: At the level of the inguinal crease, just medial to the femoral artery.

sections.p: Adjacent structures include the femoral artery and vein, the iliopsoas muscle, and the femoral canal containing Cloquet's node.

t.b: It may compress the femoral nerve, causing sensory loss.

sections.p: The femoral nerve receives arterial input from the femoral artery and its branches.
Motor fibers innervate the quadriceps, sartorius, and pectineus; sensory fibers form the medial cutaneous nerve of the thigh.
Motor: knee extension, hip flexion; Sensory: medial thigh and knee.
Common injuries include compression in the femoral canal, trauma from hip fractures, and iatrogenic damage during hip surgery.
Remember that loss of knee jerk reflex indicates femoral nerve dysfunction; the femoral triangle is a key surgical landmark.
b: Femoral triangle contains nerve, artery, vein

t.b: Femoral nerve or quadriceps muscle problem.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe weakness of the quadriceps with inability to rise from a chair
Sudden loss of knee jerk reflex
Painful swelling in the femoral triangle with sensory loss

faq.q: What causes femoral nerve palsy in childbirth?
faq.a: Pressure from the fetal head during prolonged labor can compress the nerve.

faq.q: Can a femoral hernia affect the nerve?
faq.a: Yes, a femoral hernia can compress the nerve, leading to sensory loss in the medial thigh.

faq.q: How is femoral nerve injury treated?
faq.a: Treat the underlying cause, provide physiotherapy, and avoid prolonged compression.

exam: Explain the anatomical course of the femoral nerve and its relation to the femoral artery.
Describe the clinical presentation of femoral nerve injury and how you would confirm it.
Outline the management steps for a patient with a femoral nerve injury after a hip fracture.
